summary: Dependency-confusion beacon exfiltrates host identity on npm install
details: The package's preinstall.js runs automatically on npm install and collects hostname, username, current working directory, install path, package name and version, platform, node version, and npm user-agent, then transmits those identifiers to hardcoded non-first-party destinations: an HTTPS POST and an HTTP POST to the bare IP 5.189.159.252, plus a DNS-lookup channel to an interactsh-style out-of-band domain (dae7n4pijsh1ahi9684gu8get3kaiefc9.oast.online) using hex-encoded labels built from a hardcoded token, the package name, hostname, and username. The package name and 9999.0.0 version pin are shaped to win internal-registry resolution against a private package (dependency-confusion). Self-labeling as a bug-bounty proof of concept does not change the behavior — installers whose builds resolve this name have host and user identifiers exfiltrated to attacker-designated endpoints over two independent channels (HTTPS/HTTP and DNS).

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
